document.title: U.S. Embassy Kabul Cable 000509, "Afghan Supplemental"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Framed as a personal letter to Rice, opens with a Taliban quote: 'You have all the clocks but we have all the time.' Neumann pleads for more economic and infrastructure funding to achieve victory, warning that skimping plays into Taliban strategy.

events.description: Ambassador Neumann sends a SECRET cable to the Secretary of State objecting to the supplemental decision to minimize economic assistance and omit infrastructure funding.
Neumann recommended more roads, power and agriculture assistance; the FY05 supplemental only began to reach the embassy in September.

Ambassador Neumann sends an IMMEDIATE cable to the Secretary of State objecting to the supplemental decision to minimize economic aid and exclude infrastructure, and asking for roads, power and agriculture funding.
Neumann recommends more roads, power and agriculture assistance (USD 230 million for roads and energy in the supplemental).
The FY05 supplemental funds only began to reach the embassy in September.

key_claims: A Taliban leader is quoted saying the U.S. has all the clocks but the Taliban have all the time, which frames Taliban strategy as outlasting the coalition.
Neumann argues that minimizing economic assistance and leaving out infrastructure in the supplemental plays to the Taliban strategy, not the U.S. one.
Neumann says a shortfall of about USD 400 million will not lose the war but will worsen narcotics, slow Afghan government building outside Kabul, and make the Taliban's role easier.
Neumann predicts an increase in opium poppy production next year without the proposed USD 75 million in agriculture funding.
Neumann says that without roads to reach hospitals or markets or to move troops, the Taliban message that time is on their side will resonate.
